d: Nancy Seaman, an award-winning teacher living in Farmington Hills, Michigan was accused of the 2004 hatchet/stabbing murder of her husband, Bob. She admits killing him, but says it was self-defense, claiming that he had been abusing her for years.
A report on corruption and a cover-up by city officials of Tacoma, Washington, focusing on David Brame, the city’s police chief who rose to power despite a shady past.

In 2002, dancer Catherine Woods went to New York in search of fame but became a stripper to pay the rent. She started seeing Paul Cortez while living with her ex-boyfriend David Haughn. In November 2005, she was murdered. The two men became suspects.
A man helps a new detective figure out who murdered his father.

In September 2006, Kathy Wangler, wife of anesthesiologist Dr. Mark Wangler, died from carbon monoxide poisoning in their home. Their 30-year marriage had been falling apart; In 2009, investigators concluded that Dr. Wangler had murdered his wife.

In 1996 the car which Sheila Bryan was driving with her mother as passenger accidentally veered off the road and into a ditch killing her mother. Sheila was charged withs murder -- then tried, convicted, and sentenced to life imprisonment.
The investigation of the September 24, 1988 sexual torture-murder in Louisville, Kentucky, of Brenda Sue Schaefer.

st: Murder They Wrote: The End of the Dream
d: A report on the charismatic Scott Scurlock, known as “Hollywood” because of his flamboyant style and effective use of disguises in the commission of crimes, successfully eluded capture for four years while effortlessly robbing 18 banks.

A report on Eric Smith who in August 1993, at age 13, was convicted of murdering four-year-old Derrick Robie. The child’s body was found strangled and battered with rocks near his home in Savona, N.Y.
In 1976, a gunman dressed in black murders two people and wounds two more in the Texas mansion belonging to one of the victims.
Two women fight to keep the man convicted of killing their mother over 20 years earlier in prison, though he maintains his innocence.

A report on the murder of 15-year-old Martha Moxley in Greenwich, Connecticut and the new developments in Kennedy family member Michael Skakel’s efforts to overturn his 2002 murder conviction of Moxley.

The story of sweethearts Sabrina Gonsalves and John Riggins who were brutally murdered in Davis, California, in 1980. Initially, police suspected Gerald Gallego, but he was in jail at the time of the murders.

A report on the 2007 murder of Jennifer Turner, married but separated from Dr. Kirk Turner, due to his infidelities with the family banker, Tondja Colvin.  Jennifer had filed for divorce and also brought an alienation of affection suit against Tondja.

A report on the separate disappearances in 2003 of three young women, and the investigations which not only eventually discovered the one individual who had known all three women, but led to his conviction as the killer of the three.

17-year-old Marty Tankleff was convicted of murdering his adoptive parents in their home.  Marty initially confessed, but quickly recanted.  He has fought for years for his innocence, as new witnesses have surfaced who could potentially exonerate him.
The story of David Camm, who was convicted in two murder trials -- each eventually overturned -- and was found not guilty in his third trial for the murder of his wife and two children.

Jane Neumann was found dead of a gunshot wound in the basement of her home in Hudson, Wisconsin. Jane's husband Jim originally told police Jane was murdered by an intruder and then later changed his story and said she committed suicide.

A report on the deaths of four women: Tracy Ann Roberts, Kim Raffo, Barbara Briedor, and Molly Jean Dilts, all suspected prostitutes and/or drug addicts.  They were all found on November 20, 2006, in a ditch near the Golden Key Motel in Atlantic City, NJ.
Bill Flint spent his life cheating death -- not once, not twice, but three times. His friends say this is a story of how a lot of bad things happened to a really good person.

In June 2007, Dewayne Barrentine met Tausha Fields and soon after they began living together. Tausha told him some unbelievable stories about herself – leading Barrentine to verify her stories online, which resulted in the uncovering of a homicide.
